claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page linked from the support index).
Pulumi's provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Some Pulumi providers get long-term security updates, and the provider support policy page describes which providers do.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (Provider support policy) exists.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before pulumi up or pulumi preview.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step, and Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection.
Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name and lets Pulumi replace resources by creating the replacement before deleting the old one.
Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key per stack, so encrypting the same value in different stacks yields different encrypted strings.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine; some providers use Terraform schemas, while native providers map directly to cloud APIs without Terraform schemas.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in, enabled via flag, command, or environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true.
Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic for upgrading from the immediately previous major version.
In npm, the tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For covered providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.

Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/{aws,azure,azure-native,azuread,command,docker-build,gcp,kubernetes,tls,vault}/ and the linked docs pages (/docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ anchor on best practices for maintaining provider versions, /registry/, /docs/support/getting-support/) exist.

The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs in the provider's code or direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When major N+1 ships, N becomes the new LTS major and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day, regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS provider releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a provider automatically receive patch releases as they ship; pinning to a major version is recommended.
N is the latest released major version; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 (LTS) and v1 and earlier are end of life; older majors receive no patches.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life versions (N-2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
